senses.definition: How light or dark a color looks in a work of art.
senses.example: The pale blue and the dark blue had different values.

senses.definition: A part that opens or closes to control where liquid or gas moves.
senses.example: A valve in your heart closes to keep blood from moving backward.

senses.definition: A point in a drawing where lines heading into the distance seem to meet.
senses.example: The artist drew the hall’s edges toward one vanishing point.

senses.definition: In programming, a name used to keep track of a value a program needs.
senses.example: The program keeps the team’s score in a variable.

senses.definition: A saved picture described as shapes and lines that can be drawn again at different sizes.
senses.example: The vector image of a circle stayed smooth when we made it bigger.

senses.definition: A tube that carries blood back toward the heart.
senses.example: A vein in my leg brings blood toward my heart.

senses.definition: An oval track made for bicycle racing.
senses.example: The cyclists leaned into a bend at the velodrome.

senses.definition: A thin sheet of wood that can be glued onto something or pressed together with other sheets.
senses.example: The plywood had a smooth veneer on its top layer.

senses.definition: The decision a jury or judge gives at the end of a trial.
senses.example: The judge read the verdict aloud after everyone returned.

senses.definition: One of the bones that form the spine.
senses.example: Each vertebra helps protect the spinal cord.

senses.definition: A point where sides or edges meet, like the corner of a triangle or box.
senses.example: Each vertex of the box touches three edges.

senses.definition: An official refusal to approve a plan or proposed law, or the power to refuse that approval.
senses.example: A president’s veto can stop a bill from becoming law unless enough lawmakers vote to pass it anyway.

senses.definition: To use your authority to refuse to approve something.
senses.example: A president may veto a bill after lawmakers pass it.

senses.definition: A quick back-and-forth or up-and-down movement that repeats.
senses.example: I felt the vibration of the drum when I touched its edge.

senses.definition: A substance from food or another source that your body needs in small quantities for its usual work.
senses.example: Different vegetables can supply different vitamins.

senses.definition: An opening in Earth’s surface through which hot rock, ash, and gas can escape. The word can also mean the mountain that builds up around the opening.
senses.example: The volcano’s last eruption left a new layer of rock.

senses.definition: In games such as tennis or soccer, a hit or kick made before the ball touches the ground.
senses.example: Her tennis volley went over the net before the ball had a chance to bounce.

senses.definition: To hit or kick a ball before it touches the ground.
senses.example: I stepped forward to volley the ball back.

senses.definition: A measure of the difference in electric energy per unit of charge between two places. It can help drive electric current.
senses.example: The small battery has a lower voltage than the source of power for a house.

senses.definition: The amount of space something takes up, or the amount a container can hold.
senses.example: We measured the volume of the tank in liters.
